gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-joan: Bellota Text gives every stroke a single width, leaving open, unshaded curves that look commanding and distinctive. Joan, the serif, brings hairlines neither wispy nor heavy, and that moderate touch is what makes the pairing click.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-junge: Junge is a dignified serif with generous curve gaps and strokes that thin only slightly, sitting beneath Bellota Text's uniform lines. Whole paragraphs of it flow steadily, never tiring the eye.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-kameron: Kameron is a bookish serif whose curved strokes lighten mildly toward the ends and whose curves refuse to close. Bellota Text's fixed-nib look against that modulation is the standout.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-libertinus-serif: Refined and authoritative, Libertinus Serif swells slightly on its bowls and leaves the s with an open counter. Bellota Text's skeleton lines of fixed thickness meet that faint pull in turn.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-libre-caslon-text: Libre Caslon Text is a classic serif with pen-lifted curves that leave loops unfinished and a low-key thick-thin variation. Bellota Text, a constant-width ribbon, earns its keep big and brief.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-lustria: Lustria reads traditional and authoritative, with a wide-mouthed lowercase a. Across a whole page its light strokes recede only slightly, a textured grain that Bellota Text, never swelling or thinning, simply frames.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-maitree: Bellota Text never thins its curves at the turns, so each letter keeps a bold, commanding stroke from end to end. Maitree, with hairlines half the weight of its stems, feels softer beside it.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-marcellus: Refined and literary, the rounded letters here keep a clearly open side and etched-glass weight changes. Marcellus bends gently at the turns, which sits comfortably beside Bellota Text's bent-glass-tubing look.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-martel: Martel: horseshoe-open curves and a moderate, editorial contrast. Bellota Text has no thick-thin swing at all, while Martel's stems and hairlines stay in a close ratio, so the two sit together without fuss.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-mate-sc: Bellota Text has no pressure swells to slow the eye, just open, commanding curves of constant stroke. Mate SC, the serif, rewards a modest size, where its faint nib pressure and lifted-brush curve ends stay subtle.
